appraisal_events.evidence: After the courteous "vous n'êtes pas très aimable", he raises his arm "comme un chef d'orchestre" and "il abattit sa main, en une gifle retentissante, sur la joue du journaliste"; the man pales, hesitates, "ne riposta pas", and his friends busy themselves with the wings and with a speck of dust. The narrator marvels at a gesture made "non seulement au mépris du droit des gens, mais du principe de causalité", "créé ex nihilo".
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup takes the encounter outright — the blow is unanswered and the whole group visibly declines to meet it — while the mock-heroic figuring of diplomacy giving way to war holds the act at ironic distance without cancelling his dominance.

status_effects.explanation: Everyone present yields to him where they can be seen doing it: the struck man does not answer, and his three friends each find somewhere else to look.

ambiguities: The narration both aestheticizes the blow and calls it lawless and causeless, so the local ascendancy it confers is granted in a register the passage is simultaneously mocking.
